releases.name: v0.2.0 — the Status field
releases.body:
Adds a **status** to the card: what is happening *right now*, beside the focus that says what the
session is for. Ten states, each with its own glyph, tone and motion.

```
  Wire the focus panel to the plugin tools and prove a round-trip.

  ◐ Implementing: the Status field and its icons · 4m

  3 / 5 done
```

**Motion is a claim about the world.** Only the four working states loop, and only while the session
is genuinely busy — a status claiming to be working while the session is idle is drawn static, and
its age keeps counting, so a forgotten status looks forgotten rather than convincing. The two
waiting-on-you states pulse instead of spinning, because nothing is progressing there. All of it is
suppressed under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no state relies on motion alone.

The status is the agent's to keep honest and yours to correct: click the row to open the state list,
edit the detail, or clear it.

## Upgrading

The store's task lifecycle is renamed **`lifecycle`**, freeing **`status`** for the activity. A v1
document is migrated by shape rather than by version number, so a finished task does not revert to
`active`, and the extension and plugin can be at different versions without loss.

`focus_set`'s `status` parameter is now `lifecycle` — the one breaking change to a tool.

## Install

```jsonc
{ "plugins": ["@richkershaw/openchamber-session-focus-plugin"] }
```

---

## 0.2.0 — 2026-10-20

### Added

- A **status**: what is happening right now, as a state from a fixed vocabulary plus an optional
  detail. Ten states — `planning`, `implementing`, `testing`, `reviewing`, `waiting-decision`,
  `waiting-manual`, `waiting-external`, `blocked`, `idle`, `done` — each with its own glyph, tone
  and motion.
- **Motion says whether work is really happening.** Only the four working states loop, and only
  while the session is genuinely busy: a status claiming to be working while the session is idle
  is drawn static, and its age keeps counting, so a forgotten status looks forgotten. The two
  waiting-on-you states pulse rather than spin — nothing is progressing there. All motion is
  suppressed under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and no state relies on it alone.
- **You can set it too.** Clicking the status row opens the state list and an editable detail, and
  offers a Clear. A status the agent forgot is fixable without prompting it.
- `focus_status` for the agent, and the prompt block's state list is generated from the same table
  the card draws, so the two cannot drift.

### Changed

- The store's task lifecycle is renamed **`lifecycle`**, freeing **`status`** for the activity.
  A v1 document is migrated by shape rather than by version number, so a `done` task does not
  revert to `active`, and the two halves can be at different versions without loss.
- The plugin's prompt block is titled `## Focus` rather than `## Session Focus`, matching the
  section.
- `focus_set`'s `status` parameter is now `lifecycle` — a breaking change to that tool, which is
  why the plugin goes to 0.2.0.

### Packaging

- The OpenCode plugin is now a **standalone publishable package**,
  `@richkershaw/openchamber-session-focus-plugin`, so installing the agent half is one line in
  `plugins` instead of an absolute path into this repository.
- The published bundle carries **its own copy of `shared/store.ts`** rather than importing
  across folder boundaries, so the package works with this repository out of the picture.
  `@opencode/plugin` stays a declared dependency, matching how the other published plugins do it.
- `npm run build` now builds both halves, and `npm run publish:plugin` builds and publishes the
  package. Both built artifacts are committed.
- Verified by packing the package, extracting it with no repository in reach, installing only
  its declared dependency, and driving a real agent turn through it.

### Changed

- The Work Status section is now titled **Focus** rather than **Session Focus**. The extension
  keeps the longer name on t

releases.name: v0.1.0 — Session Focus panel
releases.body:
A per-session focus card for OpenChamber: what this session is doing, the agreed actions in
implementation order, ticked off as they complete, with links to the tickets and ADRs behind
them.

Two halves over one file:

- **The card** — a section in the chat's Work Status panel, kept current by hand or by the agent.
- **The plugin** — an OpenCode v2 plugin giving the agent seven `focus_*` tools and a short
  system-prompt block naming the events at which to keep the card current.
- **The store** — one JSON file per session in the project, bundled by both halves so the format
  cannot drift.

## Install

1. **Settings → Extensions** → paste this folder's path or its git URL → approve **files**.
2. Add the plugin to `plugins` in your `opencode.json(c)`:

   ```jsonc
   { "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/OpenChamber-SessionFocusPanel/agent/plugin"] }
   ```

Requires **OpenChamber 2.3.0** or newer and **OpenCode 2.x**. Keep the repository together —
the plugin imports `shared/store.ts` so it and the card share one definition of the format.

## In this release

### The card

- One **focus** line naming the task and the approach, the agreed actions, and a `n / m done` count.
- Active actions first in implementation order, then a divider, then the completed ones — kept
  rather than removed. A newly agreed action lands above the completed block.
- A tick cycles an action **outstanding → in flight → done → outstanding**; at most one is in
  flight at a time.
- Attach a ticket, ADR or PR link to any action.
- **Copy as prompt** and **Refresh** controls in the section header.
- Hides itself when no project is open, since the store lives in the project.

### The agent

- `focus_get`, `focus_set`, `focus_add`, `focus_begin`, `focus_complete`, `focus_link`,
  `focus_drop`.
- A short block appended to the system instructions on every model call, skipped entirely for a
  session with no focus yet. Set `options.instructions: false` to turn it off.

### The store

- `.openchamber/session-focus/<sessionId>.json` — keyed by session, stored in the project.
- A lost-update guard on write: re-read before writing, verify after, replay on top of a
  competing writer's copy.
- A malformed file reads as empty rather than throwing.

## Known limits

- **Section-only**: no rail panel, no full-screen page. `background.entry` is the documented route
  to a `/focus` command and session-menu actions without one.
- The host unloads the frame when the section is collapsed, so the card rebuilds from the file on
  each mount and polls every 2.5s while visible.
- A session moved to another directory does not take its store with it, and nothing prunes
  finished focus files yet.

## Verified against

`@openchamber/sdk` 2.3.x and OpenCode **2.0.31** (`@opencode/plugin` 2.0.31 — matching the
installed server). 33 tests cover the store contract and drive the plugin's real `setup` against
a stand-in host context; the manifest is validated with the SDK's own parser, so a manifest that
would fail to install fails the build. Also exercised end to end in a real OpenCode server.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/richkershaw/OpenChamber-SessionFocusPanel/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
